title: Rung 9 -- u8, u16 and u32 over one geometry, decided against each other

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- one surface under the three index component types, which must land in the same pixels

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (doc/requirements.md I.26.14). The subject is the cube, three times over at three index widths, so E = 6 against 3 and no roll makes a non-planar hexagonal silhouette rational. I.26.14 names this case's exact arm explicitly -- a rolled triangle indexed three ways, the index width being the feature and the cube incidental -- and it is not built. The decidable claim the case already carries, that u8, u16 and u32 land in identical pixels, needs no oracle and is unaffected.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of doc/requirements.md I.26.10 applied to this subject's own bounds: direction azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.73205080756888 m, and yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. The roll is -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, derived rather than set: for an edge of irrational raster slope the perpendicular pixel-centre offsets equidistribute over +/-0.5 px, so the smallest margin over L boundary pixels is about 0.5/L and it SHRINKS as the subject grows -- measured between 2e-5 and 1.8e-3 px here, under the oracle's own 5e-3 px jitter. For a slope p/q in lowest terms the same distance is exactly 0.5/sqrt(p^2+q^2) at every pixel centre in the plane and does not depend on L at all, and tan(45deg+t) and tan(90deg+t) stay rational whenever tan t does, so a roll of rational tangent keeps a rational silhouette rational. The previous -22.5 deg maximised edge-to-AXIS angle, which is not the quantity the comparison turns on. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. This subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so what the change buys it is a different draw of the same lottery and not exactness -- a property of the subject, and the reason its class is general-position.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Emission, one colour per node, and the geometry is untouched (doc/requirements.md I.26.13). A Diffuse BSDF under a uniform environment reduces to rho*L only while no surface can be seen from another; where one can, Cycles at one sample takes ONE cosine-weighted direction per pixel and the answer is rho*L or exactly 0 -- a Bernoulli draw whose mean is the visible sky fraction, which is an ambient-occlusion estimator wearing a placement's clothes. A ShaderNodeEmission at strength 1 gathers nothing, so the world as a light, the sun's disk, a light's radius and visibility all leave at once. ONE COLOUR PER NODE because flat emission over touching bodies fuses their silhouettes: a misplaced node would hide inside the union, which is a worse instrument than the noise this replaces.

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of the emission case's acceptance. A Monte-Carlo estimator's answer depends on its seed; an emitter has no estimator, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the integral that survived.

notes: Rung 3's cube three times, differing only in the component type of the index accessor. 24 vertices fit an unsigned byte with room to spare, so all three files address exactly the same triangles and the claim is exact: zero disagreeing pixels between them, decided with no oracle in it. The oracle renders the u8 file alone -- the other two are the runner's to score against it.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
